content:
maria_support: Heads-up—received report from a customer (ACME) that an old service token may be visible in a public S3 snapshot. They pasted the snippet into the ticket. Asking for immediate remediation steps.

josh_oncall: ack. can we confirm token ID? any live requests seen? :eyes:

maria_support: token string redacted in ticket. customer included timestamped curl logs showing 2026-03-16 22:12 UTC calls using the key. they say it was in `backup-2026-03-15.tar.gz`. no obvious large-volume misuse yet.

lee_security: immediate actions: 1) create replacement token, 2) revoke compromised token, 3) check audit logs for suspicious usage, 4) advise customer on S3 lifecycle + secrets storage. i'll take logs.

maria_support: I asked customer to stop using the token and to switch to new token. They requested step-by-step for revocation + proof for compliance.

josh_oncall: steps to revoke via API quick paste:```bash
# create new token
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tokens \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDCONSOLE_API_KEY" \
  -d '{"scopes":["inference:generate"],"name":"acme-rotation-2026-03-17"}'

# revoke old token
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tokens/revoke \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDCONSOLE_API_KEY" \
  -d '{"token_id":"tok_abc123_exposed"}'
``` 

maria_support: perfect. customer asked whether revocation is immediate and whether past requests will be listed in the audit.

lee_security: revocation is effective immediately for new auth checks. requests already accepted remain in logs. for audit evidence, we can export auth events and full request headers for the window. retention note: default request logs retained 180 days; admin can request extended export via compliance@redwood.ai.

josh_oncall: to pull the relevant events quickly:```bash
# query auth events for token
curl -G https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/events \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDCONSOLE_API_KEY" \
  --data-urlencode "start=2026-03-15T00:00:00Z" \
  --data-urlencode "end=2026-03-17T23:59:59Z" \
  --data-urlencode "filter=token:tok_abc123_exposed"
``` 

maria_support: customer wants assurance around data retention & PII: they asked if any user data was captured by our logs and how to request deletion.

lee_security: clarify: our request logs capture request metadata and the text of the request when customers enable full logging. if the customer had full request logging on, request bodies may be present in logs. the compliance path: 1) we can search & produce matching log slices, 2) we can redact/delete from our hot storage, 3) ask legal/compliance for formal DSAR if required. I can draft the compliance ticket.

maria_support: they did not enable full request logging by default per their account settings (we checked). good. they asked about KMS/HSM — whether API tokens are stored encrypted and whether rotating keys affects tokens.

lee_security: API tokens are stored hashed with an HMAC and encrypted at rest. customer-managed KMS (bring-your-KMS) is supported for Private installs; hosted accounts use our KMS backed by a managed HSM. rotating KMS keys does not invalidate API tokens; tokens are verified after key rotation as we rewrap secrets. HSM details are in our security FAQ if they need attestation.

josh_oncall: additional mitigation: ask customer to restrict token scopes and IP allowlist. we also recommend short TTL tokens and use of ephemeral session tokens for services.

maria_support: customer also wanted repro steps so their security team can confirm the exposed file contained the token. they asked how to verify a token was present in a gz archive without sharing the token.

josh_oncall: give them a safe grep approach:```bash
# search for token pattern without printing matches (returns exit 0 if found)
if zgrep -qE "tok_[a-z0-9]{8,}" backup-2026-03-15.tar.gz; then
  echo "POSSIBLE_TOKEN_FOUND"
else
  echo "NO_MATCH"
fi
```

maria_support: noted. customer will run that and confirm. they also want timeline entries for their audit doc (when we created replacement key, when we revoked). can we provide discrete timestamps?

josh_oncall: yes — i'll create the replacement token at 2026-03-17T01:05:00Z and revoke at 2026-03-17T01:07:12Z, and will attach the audit event IDs.

lee_security: i'll generate a short compliance summary and include guidance on preventing future exposures: vaults (HashiCorp/Cloud KMS integrations), CI secrets scanning, S3 bucket policies, and lifecycle rules. recommend enabling token rotation and short TTLs.

maria_support: customer asked if we can rotate keys for them (they're small infra team). can we offer assisted rotation for hosted customers?

lee_security: we can offer assisted rotation as a paid ops task. i'll CC sales for an ops-eng runbook. meanwhile, we can supply step-by-step and do the revocation for them if they provide admin consent via support ticket.

incbot: Incident created: INC-2026-78 by maria_support at 2026-03-17T01:08:00Z. Assigned: lee_security.

maria_support: thanks team — i'll reply to customer with the revoke/create steps, timeline placeholders, and the grep check. ping me when audit export is ready and i'll attach to ticket. :thumbsup:
